page: Microsoft Azure L32aos_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. A key differentiator is its massive local storage capacity of 23,038 GB, which is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves top 25% ratings in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as stress-ng single-core CPU performance. It also demonstrates strong capabilities in text and image processing, alongside high-speed CPU encryption execution. However, multi-core stress-ng tests, memory bandwidth, and static web serving throughput fall within the average range. For machine learning, it delivers strong performance in LLM inference for small models, though performance scales down to average levels for medium and large models.

The L32aos_v4 offers high resource density, particularly regarding its massive local storage-to-vCPU ratio. This makes it highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring large-scale local data caching or high-capacity storage without relying solely on network-attached volumes. The combination of 256 GB of RAM and 23 TB of local storage makes this instance suitable for large relational databases, data warehousing, big data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
